pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/data/rpc.ts:54 The context's only backend is an HTTP POST to the daemon's /rpc (plus the /events socket), and a case-insensitive grep of apps/console/src/data for sql, INSERT INTO, transaction, sqlite and localStorage found no hits, so this layer owns no durable store, query language, rows or transaction boundary: the repository-over-a-store precondition of data-access does not hold here (the store lives daemon-side, e.g. crates/shadowrunr-brain/src/memory/store.rs).

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/data/rpc.ts:54 The only thing this module 'owns' is the RPC transport, not a query language; the one-module-owns-the-statements rule has nothing to govern here.
apps/console/src/data/door.ts:2 There is one decode seam (the contract door), but it decodes RPC reply bodies, not store rows; the corrupt-row policy belongs to the daemon's store.
apps/console/src/data/layer.ts:95 A mutation is one RPC call; any unit of work and its transaction boundary are daemon-side.

apps/console/src/data/paged.ts:292 useRpcMany fans out one call per params entry, which looks like N+1 at the client. But there's no store here; whether a set-shaped endpoint exists is a design question for the daemon's RPC surface.
apps/console/src/data/testing.ts:88 The tests script the transport. There's no store engine whose real behavior a test would have to exercise.
